dedupe_keys.name: journey time statistics accessibility of key services in england department for transport

description: The Department for Transport's journey time statistics measure how accessible key services are from all areas of England, as journey times by public transport and walking, by cycling and by car to food stores, primary and secondary schools and further education, GP surgeries and hospitals, town centres and employment centres. An earlier release of core accessibility indicators is also listed on data.gov.uk. Coverage is national for England. The statistics are free under the Open Government Licence and published on GOV.UK; the latest edition covers 2019 and was added in November 2021. Caveats: DfT concluded after a user engagement exercise that there is no business case to continue the series, is removing its official statistics badge and points users to its new Transport Connectivity Metric and Connectivity Tool, so the series is frozen at 2019. The travel times remain useful as a baseline for accessibility and equity analyses and for testing how network disruptions change access to services. They complement the Great Britain accessibility indicators produced by researchers and are related to the DfT road traffic counts.
